newsitem.title: USA: Ariz. Navajo 750 MW coal unit at 160 MW and rising.
newsitem.headline: Ariz. Navajo 750 MW coal unit at 160 MW and rising.

text.p: The 750 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the Navajo coal-fired power plant near Page, Ariz., was operating at 160 MW and continuing to ramp up to full power, a spokesman for the plant said late Tuesday.
The unit, which tripped off-line early Tuesday, was expected to reach full load later Tuesday evening.

Navajo's other two 750 MW units were still operating near half capacity after being curtailed over the past few days because of mild weather and weak demand for power, the Salt River Project (SRP) spokesman said.

SRP holds a 21.8 percent equity stake in the Navajo plant. Other owners include the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, Los Angeles Department of Water and Power, Arizona Public Service Co, Nevada Power Co and Tucson Electric Power Co.
